claim: Linus Torvalds is a Finnish software engineer who wrote the Linux kernel in 1991
source_quote: He's the Finnish software engineer who, in nineteen ninety-one, wrote the kernel that now runs Android phones, supercomputers, servers across the globe, and arguably the entire internet's infrastructure.

claim: In 2007, Linus Torvalds lost access to BitKeeper
source_quote: in two thousand seven, when he found himself suddenly without access to BitKeeper — the proprietary source code management tool he'd been relying on

claim: Linus Torvalds built Git in two weeks
source_quote: he built his own replacement in two weeks

claim: Git emerged from practical necessity and dissatisfaction with available alternatives
source_quote: Git emerged not from academic theorizing or corporate planning, but from raw, practical necessity and a deep dissatisfaction with every alternative available.

claim: Linus Torvalds publicly expressed contempt for CVS and Subversion
source_quote: When asked about C V S and Subversion, his contempt was immediate and public. 'C V S done right' was, in his view, an impossible slogan — because the foundation itself was flawed.

claim: Linus Torvalds spent ten years using tarballs and patches for code management
source_quote: He had spent ten years using tarballs and patches, which sounds archaic until you realise that approach at least had one virtue: it didn't lie to you about what was happening to your code.

claim: Creating a new branch in Git requires approximately 41 bytes of disk space
source_quote: Creating a new branch requires about forty-one bytes of disk space — essentially nothing.

claim: The Linux kernel has over 22,000 files
source_quote: The Linux kernel, with over twenty-two thousand files and contributions from thousands of developers, averages four and a half merges per day.

claim: The Linux kernel averages 4.5 merges per day
source_quote: The Linux kernel, with over twenty-two thousand files and contributions from thousands of developers, averages four and a half merges per day.

claim: Linus Torvalds trusts between 5 and 15 specific people in his network of trust model
source_quote: He doesn't trust everyone — he trusts five to fifteen specific people.

claim: Git can diff the entire Linux kernel in under one second on a five-year-old laptop
source_quote: Git can diff the entire Linux kernel — every single file — in under a second on a five-year-old laptop.

claim: Git uses SHA-1 hashing for integrity verification, not cryptography
source_quote: Git uses SHA one hashing for integrity, not cryptography. It's not trying to keep your code secret from adversaries. It's trying to guarantee that your data hasn't been quietly corrupted.

claim: Git tracks content, not individual files
source_quote: Git tracks content, not files. It doesn't care about individual files. It cares about the entire state of the project at any given moment.

claim: Every version of a codebase in Git is identified by a SHA-1 hash representing the entire project state
source_quote: Every version of your codebase is identified by a SHA one hash — essentially a digital fingerprint — and that fingerprint represents everything, everywhere, all at once.

claim: Git succeeded because it was designed according to principles that made sense
source_quote: Git didn't succeed because it had corporate backing or marketing budgets or institutional adoption. It succeeded because it was designed according to principles that made sense

claim: The kernel grew to 22,000 files and thousands of contributors because of Git's distributed nature
source_quote: The kernel grew to twenty-two thousand files and thousands of contributors not despite Git's distributed nature, but because of it.
